paragraphs.sourceText: When most people think of the word "education," they think of a pupil as a sort of animate sausage casing. Into this empty casing, the teachers 26 stuff "education."

But genuine education, as Socrates knew more than two thousand years ago, is not 27 the stuffings of information into a person, but rather eliciting knowledge from him; it is the 28 of what is in the mind.

"The most important part of education," once wrote William Ernest Hocking, the 29 Harvard philosopher, "is this instruction of a man in what he has inside of him. And, as Edith Hamilton has reminded us, Socrates never said, "I know, learn from me." He said, rather, "Look into your own selvers and find the 30 of truth that God has put into every heart, and that only you can kindle (点燃) to a 31 ."

In a dialogue, Socrates takes an ignorant slave boy, without a day of 32 , and proves to the amazed observers that the boy really "knows" geometry--because the principles of geometry are already in his mind, waiting to be called out.

So many of the discussions and 33 about the content of education are useless and inconclusive because they 34 what should "go into" the student rather than with what should be taken out, and how this can best be done.

The college student who once said to me, after a lecture, "I spend so much time studying that I don't have a chance to learn anything," was clearly expressing his 35 with the sausage-casing view of education.

paragraphs.sourceText: Why the Mona Lisa Stands Out
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么蒙娜丽莎脱颖而出

paragraphs.sourceText: A) Have you ever fallen for a novel and been amazed not find it on lists of great books? Or walked around a sculpture renowned as a classic, struggling to see what the fuss is about? If so, you’ve probably pondered the question a psychologist, James Cutting, asked himself：How does a work of art come to be considered great?
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 您是否曾经迷恋过一本小说，却惊讶地发现它没有出现在好书清单上？或者绕着一座被誉为经典的雕塑走来走去，努力想看看有什么大惊小怪的？如果是这样，您可能已经思考过心理学家詹姆斯·卡廷（James Cutting）问自己的问题：一件艺术品如何被认为是伟大的？

paragraphs.sourceText: B) The intuitive answer is that some works of art are just great：of intrinsically superior quality. The paintings that win prime spots in galleries, get taught in classes and reproduced in books are the ones that have proved their artistic value over time. If you can’t see they’re superior, that’s your problem. It’s an intimidatingly neat explanation. But some social scientists have been asking awkward questions of it, raising the possibility that artistic canons（名作目录）are little more than fossilised historical accidents.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 直观的答案是，有些艺术作品非常棒：具有本质上卓越的品质。那些在画廊中赢得最佳位置、在课堂上教授并在书籍中复制的画作，都是随着时间的推移证明了其艺术价值的画作。如果你看不到他们的优越性，那就是你的问题。这是一个令人生畏的简洁解释。但一些社会科学家一直在提出一些尴尬的问题，提出了艺术经典只不过是历史意外事件的化石的可能性。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Cutting, a professor at Cornell University, wondered if a psychological mechanism known as the “mere-exposure effect” played a role in deciding which paintings rise to the top of the cultural league. Cutting designed an experiment to test his hunch (直觉). Over a lecture course he regularly showed undergraduates works of impressionism for two seconds at a time. Some of the paintings were canonical, included in art-history books. Others were lesser known but of comparable quality. These were exposed four times as often. Afterwards, the students preferred them to the canonical works, while a control group of students liked the canonical ones best. Cutting’s students had grown to like those paintings more simply because they had seen them more.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 康奈尔大学教授卡廷想知道一种被称为“纯粹曝光效应”的心理机制是否在决定哪些画作跻身文化联盟之巅的过程中发挥了作用。切割设计了一个实验来检验他的直觉。在讲座中，他经常向本科生展示印象派作品，每次两秒钟。其中一些画作是经典的，包含在艺术史书籍中。其他的则鲜为人知，但质量相当。这些的曝光频率是原来的四倍。后来，学生们更喜欢它们而不是经典作品，而对照组学生则最喜欢经典作品。卡廷的学生越来越喜欢这些画作，因为他们看的次数更多了。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) Cutting believes his experiment offers a clue as to how canons are formed. He points out that the most reproduced works of impressionism today tend to have been bought by five or six wealthy and influential collectors in the late 19th century. The preferences of these men bestowed（给予）prestige on certain works, which made the works more likely to be hung in galleries and printed in collections. The fame passed down the years, gaining momentum from mere exposure as it did so. The more people were exposed to, the more they liked it, and the more they liked it, the more it appeared in books, on posters and in big exhibitions. Meanwhile, academics and critics created sophisticated justifications for its preeminence（卓越） After all, it’s not just the masses who tend to rate what they see more often more highly. As contemporary artists like Warhol and Damien Hirst have grasped, critics5 praise is deeply entwined (交织）with publicity. “Scholars”, Cutting argues, “are no different from the public in the effects of mere exposure.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) Cutting 相信他的实验提供了关于经典如何形成的线索。他指出，当今印象派复制品最多的作品往往被 19 世纪末五六位富有且有影响力的收藏家购买。这些人的偏好赋予某些作品以威望，从而使这些作品更有可能悬挂在画廊中并印刷在收藏品中。名声历经数年，仅因曝光而获得动力。人们接触的越多，就越喜欢它，越喜欢它，它就越多地出现在书籍、海报和大型展览中。与此同时，学者和评论家为它的卓越性创造了复杂的理由。毕竟，不仅仅是大众倾向于对他们经常看到的东西给予更高的评价。正如沃霍尔和达明安·赫斯特等当代艺术家所认识到的那样，批评家的赞扬与宣传紧密地交织在一起。卡廷认为，“学者”与公众在单纯曝光的效果上没有什么不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The process described by Cutting evokes a principle that the sociologist Duncan Watts calls“cumulative advantage”：once a thing becomes popular，it will tend to become more popular still. A few years ago, Watts, who is employed by Microsoft to study the dynamics of social networks, had a similar experience to Cutting‘s in another Paris museum. After queuing to see the“Mona Lisa”in its climate- controlled bulletproof box at the Louvre, he came away puzzled：why was it considered so superior to the three other Leonardos in the previous chamber, to which nobody seemed to be paying the slightest attention?
paragraphs.translationZh: E) Cutting 所描述的过程引出了社会学家邓肯·瓦茨 (Duncan Watts) 称之为“累积优势”的原则：一旦某种事物变得流行，它就会变得更加流行。几年前，受雇于微软研究社交网络动态的瓦茨在巴黎的另一家博物馆也有过与卡廷类似的经历。在卢浮宫排队观看装在恒温防弹箱里的《蒙娜丽莎》后，他感到困惑：为什么它被认为比前一个房间里的其他三幅列奥纳多作品更优秀，而似乎没有人对这幅画有丝毫关注？

paragraphs.sourceText: F) When Watts looked into the history of“the greatest painting of all time”,he discovered that, for most of its life, the “Mona Lisa’’ remained in relative obscurity. In the 1850s, Leonardo da Vinci was considered no match for giants of Renaissance art like Titian and Raphael, whose works were worth almost ten times as much as the “Mona Lisa”. It was only in the 20th century that Leonardo’s portrait of his patron5s wife rocketed to the number-one spot. What propelled it there wasn’t a scholarly re- evaluation, but a theft.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 当瓦茨研究“有史以来最伟大的画作”的历史时，他发现，在其一生的大部分时间里，《蒙娜丽莎》一直处于相对默默无闻的状态。 1850年代，达芬奇被认为无法与提香和拉斐尔等文艺复兴艺术巨匠相比，他们的作品价值几乎是《蒙娜丽莎》的十倍。直到20世纪，列奥纳多为他的赞助人妻子创作的肖像画才飙升至第一名。推动它出现的不是学术上的重新评估，而是盗窃。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) In 1911 a maintenance worker at the Louvre walked out of the museum with the “Mona Lisa”, hidden under his smock (工作服). Parisians were shocked at the theft of a painting to which, until then, they had paid little attention. When the museum reopened, people queued to see the gap where the “Mona Lisa “, had once hung in a way they had never done for the painting “Mona Lisa “ ，came to represent Western culture itself. itself. From then on, the
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 1911年，卢浮宫的一名维修工人将藏在工作服下的《蒙娜丽莎》走出博物馆。巴黎人对一幅画被盗感到震惊，在此之前他们很少关注这幅画。当博物馆重新开放时，人们排队参观《蒙娜丽莎》的缺口，曾经以一种他们从未做过的方式悬挂着《蒙娜丽莎》，这幅画开始代表西方文化本身。本身。从此，

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Although many have tried., it does Seem improbable that the painting‘s unique status can be attributed entirely to the quality of its brushstrokes. It has been said that the subjects eyes follow the viewer around the room. But as the painting’s biographer, Donald Sassoon, dryly notes, “In reality the effect can be obtained from any portrait. ’’ Duncan Watts proposes that the “Mona Lisa” is merely an extreme example of a general rule. Paintings? poems and pop songs are buoyed （使浮起）or sunk by random events or preferences that turn into waves of influence, passing down the generations.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 尽管很多人都尝试过，但这幅画的独特地位似乎不太可能完全归因于其笔触的质量。据说受试者的眼睛会跟随观察者在房间里四处走动。但正如这幅画的传记作者唐纳德·沙逊干巴巴地指出的那样，“实际上，从任何肖像中都可以获得这种效果。”邓肯·瓦茨提出，《蒙娜丽莎》只是一般规则的一个极端例子。绘画、诗歌和流行歌曲会因随机事件或偏好而浮起或沉没，这些事件或偏好会变成影响波，代代相传。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) “Saying that cultural objects have value,”Brian Eno once wrote,“ like saying that telephones have conversations”.Nearly all the cultural objects we consume arrive wrapped in inherited opinion；our preferences are always, to some extent, someone else’s. Visitors to the “Mona Lisa” know they are about to visit the greatest work of art ever and come away appropriately impressed—or let down. An audience at a performance of“Hamlet”, know it is regarded as a work of genius, so that is what they mostly see. Watts even calls the preeminence of Shakespeare a “historical accident”.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) “说文物有价值，”布莱恩·伊诺曾经写道，“就像说电话可以通话一样。”我们消费的几乎所有文物都包含着继承的观点；在某种程度上，我们的偏好总是别人的。参观《蒙娜丽莎》的游客知道他们即将参观有史以来最伟大的艺术作品，并在离开时留下适当的印象或失望。观看《哈姆雷特》演出的观众知道它被视为天才之作，所以这就是他们看到的最多的东西。瓦茨甚至称莎士比亚的卓越地位是“历史的偶然”。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Although the rigid high-low distinction fell apart in the 1960s, we still use culture as a badge of identity. Today’s fashion for eclecticism (折中主义）一“I love Bach, Abba and Jay Z”-is, Shamus Khan, a Columbia University psychologist, argues, a new way for the middle class to distinguish themselves from what they perceive to be the narrow tastes of those beneath them in the social hierarchy.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 尽管严格的高低区分在 20 世纪 60 年代已经瓦解，但我们仍然使用文化作为身份的徽章。哥伦比亚大学心理学家沙姆斯·汗 (Shamus Khan) 认为，当今流行的折中主义——“我爱巴赫、阿巴和杰伊·Z”——是中产阶级将自己与他们认为的社会等级中处于下层的狭隘品味区分开来的一种新方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) The intrinsic quality of a work of art is starting to seem like its least important attribute. But perhaps it’s more significant than our social scientists allow. First of all, a work needs a certain quality to be eligible to be swept to the top of the pile. The “Mona Lisa” may not be a worthy world champion, but it was in the Louvre in the first place, and not by accident. Secondly, some stuff is simply better than other stuff. Read “Hamlet” after reading even the greatest of Shakespeare’s contemporaries, and the difference may strike you as unarguable.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 一件艺术品的内在品质开始看起来像是它最不重要的属性。但也许它比我们的社会科学家所认为的更重要。首先，一部作品需要具备一定的品质，才有资格跻身榜首。 《蒙娜丽莎》也许不是当之无愧的世界冠军，但它首先出现在卢浮宫，而且并非偶然。其次，有些东西就是比其他东西更好。在读完莎士比亚同时代最伟大的作家之后再读《哈姆雷特》，你可能会觉得其中的差异是无可争议的。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) A study in the British Journal of Aesthetics suggests that the exposure effect doesn’t work the same way on everything, and points to a different conclusion about how canons are formed. The social scientists are right to say that we should be a little sceptical of greatness, and that we should always look in the next room. Great art and mediocrity(平庸) can get confused, even by experts. But that‘s why we need to see, and read, as much as we can. The more we5re exposed to the good and the bad, the better we are at telling the difference. The eclecticists have it.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 《英国美学杂志》上的一项研究表明，曝光效应对所有事物的作用并不相同，并就经典如何形成提出了不同的结论。社会科学家说我们应该对伟大持怀疑态度，并且我们应该总是看看隔壁房间，这是正确的。即使对于专家来说，伟大的艺术和平庸也会被混淆。但这就是为什么我们需要尽可能多地去看、去读。我们接触到的好和坏的东西越多，我们就越能区分它们。折衷主义者有它。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. According to Duncan Watts, the superiority of the “Mona Lisa” ，to Leonardo’s other works resulted from the cumulative advantage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 按照邓肯·瓦茨的说法，《蒙娜丽莎》相对于列奥纳多其他作品的优越性是累积优势的结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Some social scientists have raised doubts about the intrinsic value of certain works of art.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 一些社会科学家对某些艺术作品的内在价值提出了质疑。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. It is often random events or preferences that determine the fate of a piece of art.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 决定一件艺术品的命运的往往是随机事件或偏好。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. In his experiment, Cutting found that his subjects liked lesser known works better than canonical works because of more exposure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 在他的实验中，卡廷发现他的受试者比经典作品更喜欢鲜为人知的作品，因为它们的曝光率更高。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. The author thinks the greatness of an art work still lies in its intrinsic value.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 笔者认为一件艺术作品的伟大之处仍然在于它的内在价值。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. It is true of critics as well as ordinary people that the popularity of artistic works is closely associated with publicity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 对于批评家和普通人来说，艺术作品的流行与宣传密切相关，这都是事实。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. We need to expose ourselves to more art and literature in order to tell the superior from the inferior.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52、我们需要多接触艺术和文学，才能辨别优劣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. A study of the history of the greatest paintings suggests even a great work of art could experience years of neglect.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 对最伟大绘画历史的研究表明，即使是一件伟大的艺术作品也可能经历多年的忽视。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. Culture is still used as a mark to distinguish one social class from another.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 文化仍然被用作区分一个社会阶层与另一个社会阶层的标志。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. Opinions about and preferences for cultural objects are often inheritable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 对文物的看法和偏好往往是可以继承的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: When the right person is holding the right job at the right moment, that person’s influence is greatly expanded. That is the position in which Janet Yellen, who is expected to be confirmed as the next chair of the Federal Reserve Bank (Fed) in January, now finds herself. If you believe, as many do, that unemployment is the major economic and social concern of our day, then it is no stretch to think Yellen is the most powerful person in the world right now.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当合适的人在合适的时候担任合适的工作时，这个人的影响力就会大大扩大。这就是珍妮特·耶伦（Janet Yellen）现在所处的位置，她预计将在一月份被确认为下一任美联储主席。如果你像许多人一样相信失业是当今主要的经济和社会问题，那么毫不夸张地说，耶伦是当今世界上最有权势的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Throughout the 2008 financial crisis and the recession and recovery that followed, central banks have taken on the role of stimulators of last resort, holding up the global economy with vast amounts of money in the form of asset buying. Yellen, previously a Fed vice chair, was one of the principal architects of the Fed $3.8 trillion money dump. A star economist known for her groundbreaking work on labor markets, Yellen was a kind of prophetess early on in the crisis for her warnings about the subprime (次级债)meltdown. Now it will be her job to get the Fed and the markets out of the biggest and most unconventional monetary program in history without derailing the fragile recovery.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在2008年金融危机以及随后的衰退和复苏期间，各国央行一直扮演着最后刺激者的角色，以资产购买的形式提供大量资金，支撑着全球经济。耶伦曾担任美联储副主席，是美联储 3.8 万亿美元转储资金的主要设计者之一。耶伦是一位以其在劳动力市场方面的开创性工作而闻名的明星经济学家，她在危机初期就发出了关于次级债崩溃的警告，堪称一位女预言家。现在，她的工作是让美联储和市场退出历史上规模最大、最非常规的货币计划，同时又不破坏脆弱的复苏。

paragraphs.sourceText: The good news is that Yellen, 67, is particularly well suited to meet these challenges. She has a keen understanding of financial markets, an appreciation for their imperfections and a strong belief that human suffering was more related to unemployment than anything else.
paragraphs.translationZh: 好消息是，67 岁的耶伦特别适合应对这些挑战。她对金融市场有敏锐的了解，认识到金融市场的缺陷，并坚信人类的痛苦与失业的关系比其他任何因素都更重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some experts worry that Yellen will be inclined to chase unemployment to the neglect of inflation. But with wages still relatively flat and the economy increasingly divided between the well-off and the long-term unemployed, more people worry about the opposite, deflation (通货紧缩）that would aggravate the economy’s problems.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一些专家担心耶伦将倾向于追逐失业而忽视通胀。但由于工资仍然相对持平，经济中富裕阶层和长期失业阶层之间的分化日益加剧，更多人担心相反的通货紧缩会加剧经济问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Either way, the incoming Fed chief will have to walk a fine line in slowly ending the stimulus. It must be steady enough to deflate bubbles(去泡沫) and bring markets back down to earth but not so quick that it creates another credit crisis.
paragraphs.translationZh: 无论哪种方式，即将上任的美联储主席都必须谨慎行事，慢慢结束刺激计划。它必须足够稳定，以消除泡沫并使市场回归现实，但又不能太快，以免造成另一场信贷危机。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unlike many past Fed leaders, Yellen is not one to buy into the finance industry‘s argument that it should be left alone to regulate itself. She knows all along the Fed has been too slack on regulation of finance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 与许多过去的美联储领导人不同，耶伦并不认同金融业应自行监管的观点。她知道美联储在金融监管方面一直过于松懈。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yellen is likely to address the issue right after she pushes unemployment below 6%, stabilizes markets and makes sure that the recovery is more inclusive and robust. As Princeton Professor Alan Blinder says, “She’s smart as a whip, deeply logical, willing to argue but also a good listener. She can persuade without creating hostility”All those traits will be useful as the global economy‘s new power player takes on its most annoying problems. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 耶伦可能会在将失业率降至 6% 以下、稳定市场并确保复苏更具包容性和强劲后立即解决这个问题。正如普林斯顿大学教授艾伦·布林德所说，“她聪明如鞭，逻辑严密，愿意争论，但也是一个很好的倾听者。她可以说服人而不产生敌意。”当全球经济的新权力参与者解决最恼人的问题时，所有这些特征都将发挥作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Air pollution is deteriorating in many places around the world. The fact that public parks in cities become crowded as soon as the sun shines proves that people long to breathe in green, open spaces. They do not all know what they are seeking but they flock there, nevertheless. And, in these surroundings, they are generally both peaceful and peaceable. It is rare to see people fighting in a garden. Perhaps struggle unfolds first, not at an economic or social level, but over the appropriation of air, essential to life itself. If human beings can breathe and share air, they don^ need to struggle with one another.
paragraphs.translationZh: 世界许多地方的空气污染正在恶化。城市的公园一出太阳就变得拥挤，这一事实证明人们渴望在绿色、开放的空间里呼吸。他们并不都知道自己在寻找什么，但尽管如此，他们还是聚集在那里。而且，在这些环境中，他们总体上都是安宁祥和的。很少看到有人在花园里打架。也许斗争首先展开，不是在经济或社会层面，而是在对生命本身至关重要的空气的占有上。如果人类能够呼吸并分享空气，他们就不需要彼此斗争。

paragraphs.sourceText: Unfortunately, in our western tradition, neither materialist nor idealist theoreticians give enough consideration to this basic condition for life. As for politicians, despite proposing curbs on environmental pollution, they have not yet called for it to be made a crime. Wealthy countries are even allowed to pollute if they pay for it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 不幸的是，在我们的西方传统中，唯物主义和唯心主义理论家都没有对生命的这一基本条件给予足够的考虑。至于政界人士，尽管提出遏制环境污染，但尚未呼吁将其定为犯罪。富裕国家甚至可以允许污染，只要他们为此付出代价。

paragraphs.sourceText: But is our life worth anything other than money? The plant world shows us in silence what faithfulness to life consists of. It also helps us to a new beginning, urging us to care for our breath, not only at a vital but also at a spiritual level. The interdependence to which we must pay the closest attention is that which exists between ourselves and the plant world. Often described as “the lungs of the planet” the woods that cover the earth offer us the gift of breathable air by releasing oxygen. But their capacity to renew the air polluted by industry has long reached its limit. If we lack the air necessary for a healthy life, it is because we have filled it with chemicals and undercut the ability of plants to regenerate it. As we know, rapid deforestation combined with the massive burning of fossil fuels is an explosive recipe for an irreversible disaster.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但除了金钱之外，我们的生命还有其他价值吗？植物世界默默地向我们展示了什么是对生命的忠诚。它还帮助我们进入一个新的开始，敦促我们不仅在生命层面而且在精神层面上照顾我们的呼吸。我们必须密切关注的相互依存关系是我们与植物世界之间存在的相互依存关系。覆盖地球的森林通常被称为“地球之肺”，通过释放氧气为我们提供可呼吸的空气。但它们更新工业污染空气的能力早已达到极限。如果我们缺乏健康生活所需的空气，那是因为我们在其中充满了化学物质，削弱了植物再生空气的能力。众所周知，快速砍伐森林加上大量燃烧化石燃料是导致不可逆转灾难的爆炸性因素。

paragraphs.sourceText: The fight over the appropriation of resources will lead the entire planet to hell unless humans learn to share life, both with each other and with plants. This task is simultaneously ethical and political because it can be discharged only when each takes it upon herself or himself and only when it is accomplished together with others. The lesson taught by plants is that sharing life expands and enhances the sphere of the living, while dividing life into so-called natural or human resources diminishes it. We must come to view the air, the plants and ourselves as the contributors to the preservation of life and growth, rather than a web of quantifiable objects or productive potentialities at our disposal. Perhaps then we would finally begin to live, rather than being concerned with bare survival. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 除非人类学会彼此以及与植物分享生命，否则资源争夺的斗争将把整个地球带入地狱。这项任务同时具有伦理性和政治性，因为只有当每个人自己承担并与他人共同完成时，它才能完成。植物给我们的教训是，分享生命可以扩大和增强生命的范围，而将生命划分为所谓的自然或人力资源则会缩小生命的范围。我们必须将空气、植物和我们自己视为维持生命和生长的贡献者，而不是我们可以支配的可量化物体或生产潜力的网络。也许那时我们终于可以开始生活了，而不是仅仅关心生存。
